minimum_sufficient_response: Pseudocode: transfer(s,d,a): if s==d return fail; first=min(s,d); second=max(s,d); lock(first); lock(second); if balance[s]>=a: balance[s]-=a; balance[d]+=a; unlock(second); unlock(first); return success; else unlock(second); unlock(first); return fail. Reads/checks/updates: balance[s] is read and checked while holding lock(s); balance[d] is updated while holding lock(d); both locks are held during the check-and-update so no other transfer can interleave between check and update. Correctness: mutual exclusion follows because any transfer touching an account holds that account's lock; no overdraft follows because the check and debit occur under the source lock and no other transfer can change the source balance between them; total balance is preserved because a successful transfer subtracts a from source and adds a to destination, and a failed transfer changes nothing; deadlock freedom follows because all transfers acquire locks in the same global order by account ID, so a cycle in the wait-for graph would require an account ID to be both smaller and larger than another. Concrete deadlock example for wrong locking: T1 transfers A to B and locks A then waits for B; T2 transfers B to A and locks B then waits for A. Each holds one lock and waits for the other, so neither can proceed.
